sentences.text:
This Misc. Appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act has been filed against the Award dated 13.09.2013 passed by Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Panna in M.A.C.C. No.
75/2012.
2.

The facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short are that on 16.05.2012, the injured and deceased persons after loading their goods were coming to Krashi Mandi, Katni by Truck No.MP-20-GA-4990.
The Driver of the offending Truck bearing registration No.MP-20-GA-4990 by driving the truck in a rash and negligent manner turned the Truck up side down, as a result the claimant sustained injuries.
The Claims Tribunal held the Insurance Company liable for the reason that the injured was traveling in a goods carriage along with his goods, therefore, there is no violation of insurance policy.

3. Challenging the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal, it is submitted by the counsel for the appellant that the respondent no.1 has admitted in his evidence that he was sitting on the Gunny bags loaded on the truck and was not sitting in the cabin of the truck and therefore, in the light of judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Cholleti Bharatamma, reported in (2008) 1 SCC 423, Insurance Company is not liable.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Cholleti Bharatamma, reported in (2008) 1 SCC 423
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. It is submitted by the counsel for the respondent no.1 that the observation made by the Supreme Court in the case of Cholleti Bharatamma (supra) is obiter dicta and does not lay down the correct preposition of law.
5.

The only question for consideration is as to whether the respondent No.1/claimant was traveling in the cabin of the truck or he was sitting on his goods loaded on the offending truck?
6.
The respondent no.1 in paragraph 13 of his cross-examination has admitted that he was sitting on the Gunny bags loaded on back of the truck.
Thus, it is clear that the respondent no.1/claimant was not sitting in the cabin of the truck.

7. The Supreme Court in the case of Cholleti Bharatamma (supra) has held as under:-

2 "19.

entities.text: Branch Manager,Hdfc Ergo General ... vs Charan Das Patel
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is now well settled that the owner of the goods means only the person who travels in the cabin of the vehicle."

8. Since, the respondent No.1/claimant was not traveling in the cabin of the truck but was sitting on his goods loaded on the truck, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Insurance Company was wrongly held to be jointly responsible to pay compensation along with driver and owner of the truck.
9. Accordingly, the Insurance Company/appellant is exonerated from its liability.

10. The Full Bench of Madras High Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Nagammal .

entities.text:
United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Nagammal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Nagammal and others, reported in 2009 ACJ 865 has held that in such case the Principle of Pay and Recover cannot be applied.
11. As a consequence thereof, the award dated 13.09.2013 passed by Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Panna in M.A.C.C. No. 75/2012 is modified to the extent mentioned above.
12. The appeal succeeds and is allowed.

(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE TG/-
